content:
1 Safety
Read this manual before the unit is started for the first time. The unit delivers compressed air at a pressure that can injure; isolate it from the air system and lock the supply off before any part of it is opened.

Only a trained technician may change a controller setting or open the oil circuit. The oil and the airend stay hot for a long time after a stop.

3 Controller messages
The controller shows one message at a time. A warning leaves the unit running, a shutdown warning announces a limit that is close, and a shutdown stops the unit and inhibits a restart until it is reset by hand.

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: W101 | Type: Warning | Message: Line pressure low | Trigger: Low-pressure switch closed in any state | Threshold: 7.0 bar | Delay: 10 s | Reset: Automatic

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: W102 | Type: Warning | Message: Continuous load time exceeded | Trigger: Loaded without reaching cut-out | Threshold: 10 min | Delay: 2 min | Reset: Automatic

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: W104 | Type: Warning | Message: Oil temperature high | Trigger: Oil temperature above the warning setting while running | Threshold: 75 °C | Delay: 5 min | Reset: Automatic

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: W108 | Type: Warning | Message: Motor starts per hour exceeded | Trigger: More starts in one hour than the setting allows | Threshold: 6 per hour | Delay: 0 s | Reset: Automatic

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: X201 | Type: Shutdown warning | Message: Oil temperature very high | Trigger: Oil temperature above the shutdown warning setting while running | Threshold: 85 °C | Delay: 30 s | Reset: Automatic

3 Controller messages — Controller messages
Code: S301 | Type: Shutdown | Message: Oil temperature shutdown | Trigger: Oil temperature above the shutdown setting while running | Threshold: 95 °C | Delay: 5 s | Reset: Manual

4 Programmable settings
The controller refuses a value outside the range below, and it refuses a value that would put two settings in the wrong order.

4 Programmable settings — Programmable settings
Parameter: Cut-in pressure | Unit: bar | Min: 5.0 | Default: 8.0 | Max: 9.5

4 Programmable settings — Programmable settings
Parameter: Cut-out pressure | Unit: bar | Min: 6.0 | Default: 10.0 | Max: 11.0

4 Programmable settings — Programmable settings
Parameter: Oil temperature warning | Unit: °C | Min: 60 | Default: 75 | Max: 90

4 Programmable settings — Programmable settings
Parameter: Maximum starts per hour | Unit: per hour | Min: 1 | Default: 6 | Max: 12

8.1 Before you start
Work from what the unit shows, not from what it is said to do. Read the controller message list first, then the signals of the pneumatic panel, and only then open a component. A message names a limit that was crossed; it does not name the cause, and the same message follows from several of the causes listed in 8.2.

Let the unit run through one full load and unload cycle before a reading is taken. Oil temperature settles slowly, so a reading taken within ten minutes of a start says little about the cooling circuit. (Do not exceed 95 °C (203 °F): above that limit the controller stops the unit and inhibits the restart.)

8.1 Before you start
• Note the controller message, the state of the unit and the hour reading before anything is changed. • Take every pressure from the pneumatic panel, never from a temporary gauge in the distribution line. • Change one thing at a time and repeat the reading after one full cycle.

8.2 Fault tables
Each table below lists the causes of one condition, the signals that move, what to check and what to do. A cause that explains more than one condition keeps the same fault id under each of them.

8.2.1 Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure
The unit runs but the line pressure stays below the cut-in setting, and the low-pressure switch closes.

section_title: Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
content:
8.2.2 Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
The unit loads and unloads more often than the setting allows, and the starts per hour message appears.

8.2.1 Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure — Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure
Fault id: downstream_air_leak | Possible cause: Downstream air leak. Air escapes from the distribution line after the unit, and the unit makes the loss up. Raises W101. | Subsystem: distribution | Signals: Line pressure (P2) falls faster than usual while unloaded. Load cycle rate is higher. | Checks: 1. Close the isolation valve at the reservoir outlet. 2. Watch line pressure (P2) for ten minutes with the unit stopped. 3. Walk the distribution line and listen at every joint. | Remedy: Repair the leaking joint or fitting and put the line back in service.

8.2.1 Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure — Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure
Fault id: intake_filter_clogged | Possible cause: Intake filter clogged. The filter element is loaded with dust and restricts the air the element draws. Raises W101. | Subsystem: intake unloading | Signals: Line pressure (P2) is low while loaded. Motor current (I1) is low while loaded. | Checks: 1. Read the filter restriction indicator. 2. Inspect the element against a lamp. 3. Compare motor current (I1) with the value of a clean element. | Remedy: Fit a new intake filter element and reset the service counter.

8.2.1 Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure — Line pressure below setpoint low_line_pressure
Fault id: dryer_purge_leak | Possible cause: Dryer purge leak. The purge valve does not seat, so regeneration air escapes without stopping. Raises W101 and W102. | Subsystem: dryer | Signals: Purge pressure (P4) is high while loaded. Line pressure (P2) falls while loaded. | Checks: 1. Listen at the purge silencer with the unit loaded. 2. Read purge pressure (P4) over one full tower period. 3. Check the purge valve seat and its pilot line. | Remedy: Overhaul or replace the purge valve and repeat the check.

8.2.3 Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high
The oil temperature reading stays above the warning setting, and the unit may reach the shutdown limit.

section_title: Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
content:
8.2.2 Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling — Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
Fault id: downstream_air_leak | Possible cause: Downstream air leak. The same leak makes the unit load again soon after it unloads. Raises W108. | Subsystem: distribution | Signals: Load cycle rate is higher. Line pressure (P2) falls faster than usual while unloaded. | Checks: 1. Record the number of starts in one hour. 2. Close the outlet isolation valve and watch line pressure (P2). 3. Walk the distribution line and listen at every joint. | Remedy: Repair the leaking joint or fitting and put the line back in service.

section_title: Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
content:
8.2.2 Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling — Compressor starts and loads too often frequent_cycling
Fault id: reservoir_isolation_valve_closed | Possible cause: Reservoir isolation valve closed. Part of the reservoir volume is shut off, so the unit cycles on a small volume. Raises W108. | Subsystem: reservoirs | Signals: Load cycle rate is higher. Line pressure (P2) rises faster than usual while loaded. | Checks: 1. Check the position of every reservoir isolation valve. 2. Compare the reservoir pressure with line pressure (P2). 3. Time one loaded run. | Remedy: Open the isolation valve and lock it in the open position.

8.2.3 Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high — Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high
Fault id: oil_cooler_fouled | Possible cause: Oil cooler fouled. The cooler matrix is blocked with dust, so it rejects less heat than it should. Raises W104 and X201. | Subsystem: cooling | Signals: Oil temperature (T1) rises gradually in every state. | Checks: 1. Inspect the cooler matrix against a lamp. 2. Check the cooling air path for obstructions. 3. Read oil temperature (T1) after one hour at full load. | Remedy: Clean the cooler matrix with the cleaning kit and repeat the reading.

8.2.3 Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high — Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high
Fault id: high_ambient_temperature | Possible cause: No fault: high ambient temperature. The cooling air is warmer than the reference condition, so the oil settles higher. Raises W104. | Subsystem: cooling | Signals: Oil temperature (T1) is high in every state. | Checks: 1. Read the temperature of the cooling air at the inlet. 2. Compare it with the reference conditions. 3. Check that warm exhaust air is not drawn back in. | Remedy: Improve the ventilation of the machine room or shade the air inlet.

8.2.3 Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high — Oil temperature high oil_temperature_high
Fault id: oil_filter_clogged | Possible cause: Oil filter clogged. The filter element restricts the oil flow to the airend, so less heat leaves with the oil. Raises W104 and S301. | Subsystem: oil | Signals: Oil temperature (T1) rises gradually while loaded. | Checks: 1. Read the filter restriction indicator. 2. Check the hours since the last oil filter change. 3. Read oil temperature (T1) at full load. | Remedy: Fit a new oil filter element and reset the service counter.
